scoring_justification: The workflow outputs computed analytical tables. Full recompute is infeasible without duplicating the IAPWS implementation; therefore we compare reported values to paper gold with tolerances and enforce a monotonicity constraint on the sweep.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold reference values for Wilson-point properties and the ΔT_W vs k_p sweep
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Wilson-point values from paper Table 1 (ΔT_W=35.1 K, N_W=2.46e18, r_30=2.69 nm, r_32=3.67 nm, Y_W=0.0002). Sweep values from the reference oracle solve.sh, consistent with the paper’s analytical model.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Wilson-point values extracted from paper Table 1; sweep values generated by the analytical solution (same model as the paper) and recorded in solve.sh.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact paper‑reported analytical values; the sweep values correspond to a correct implementation of the paper’s model and match the trend shown in Figure 2.

outputs.description: Wilson-point properties computed from the analytical solution at p_W = 0.1 bar, k_p = 1000 s⁻¹.
Maximum subcooling as a function of expansion rate at p_W = 0.1 bar, with a monotonic increase.

output_contract.notes: All properties are derived from the analytical model. Numerical integration for validation is not part of the scored reproduction.
